figures.finding: Screen Ireland lends up to 70% of an Irish fiction feature's budget to a maximum of €950,000 when the budget is €3 million or less, up to 65% between €1 million and €1.2 million for €3–7 million budgets, and up to 65% to a maximum of €1.3 million for €7–20 million (up to €100,000 more with a female writer or director); development funding stops at €125,000 per project, and total state aid is held to 50% of cost unless the film is low-budget (€3 million or less) or difficult.

value.form: limited-recourse loans recoupable pro rata pari passu with other equity

figures.applies: Ireland, Screen Ireland Fiction: Irish Production (feature films, animation features included), limits read 2026-11-01; non-Irish writers or directors get significantly less.

sources.said: the amount of state aid used to finance a film project may not exceed 50% of its total cost, subject to, inter alia, where the film is considered to be ‘low budget' or ‘difficult' … A film may be considered ‘low budget’ if its production budget does not exceed €3 million. … The maximum amount of Screen Ireland development funding that can be provided to any one project is €125,000. … For projects with budgets of up to €3 million … Screen Ireland can provide up to 70% of the budget with a maximum of €950,000 … For projects with budgets of over €3 million and not more than €7 million … Screen Ireland can provide up to 65% of the budget, between €1,000,000 and €1,200,000 … For projects with budgets of over €7 million and not more than €20 million … Screen Ireland can provide up to 65% of the budget, with a maximum of €1,300,000 … enhanced production funding of up to an additional €100,000 is available to projects with Female Talent (writer and/or director, writer/director) attached … but will not normally exceed €350,000 per project.

Funding is provided in the form of limited-recourse loans recoverable from a share of revenues from the exploitation of the project and also entitling Screen Ireland to a share of net profits. … All projects in receipt of Screen Ireland funding must provide and allow for a contingency of 10% of the submitted production budget. … Screen Ireland requires a 1.5:1 spend ratio on its investment.

figures.finding: On a Screen Ireland-funded film the Irish producer, writer and director share a 60% recoupment corridor, with 10% each to an Irish director and an Irish writer (45% to the company if only one of them is Irish, 50% if neither is).

value.note: the guidelines' list leaves the company's share blank when both are Irish; 0.40 is 60% less the two 10% shares

figures.applies: Ireland, Screen Ireland production funding of features, TV drama, documentary and animation.

sources.said: are entitled to share in a recoupment corridor of 60% subject to certain terms and conditions. … 10% to Irish Director, and … 10% to Irish Writer. … 45% to Production Company, … In the event that neither the writer nor director are Irish the recoupment corridor shall simply be 50% to the Production Company.

figures.finding: Since 20 May 2025 a feature with qualifying expenditure under €20 million and an EEA national or resident in a key creative role can take Section 481 at 40% (the 'Scéal uplift') instead of 32%, the higher rate applied on completion.
figures.applies: Ireland, enhanced Section 481 credit for lower-budget film (Finance Act 2024; S.I. 197 of 2025); the 32% standard credit and €125m cap are held in world.json.

sources.said: The enhanced credit can apply only to qualifying films certified on, or after, 20 May 2025. … An enhanced rate of 40% may apply to the film Corporation Tax Credit for qualifying lower budget films, where: … the qualifying expenditure on the film is less than €20 million … one or more of the key creative roles is performed by an individual who is either a national of, or ordinarily resident in, a European Economic Area (EEA) State. … On completion, if the qualifying film meets the criteria for the enhanced credit, the value of the credit is calculated using the 40% rate.

figures.finding: Revenue accepts producer-related fees (producer, co-producer, executive producer and company overhead) as eligible for Section 481 up to 15% of the global budget when eligible spending is over 80% of it, or 10% when it is under 80%; higher only if substantiated at arm's length.
figures.applies: Ireland, Section 481, Revenue Tax and Duty Manual Part 15-02-04 (last reviewed August 2026).

sources.said: These fees will be categorised in the budget as including “Producer”, “Co- Producer”, “Executive Producer” fees and “Production/Overhead” corporate fees. … that the eligible producer-related fees do not exceed 15% of the global budget where the eligible expenditure is in excess of 80% of the global budget; or … that the eligible producer-related fees do not exceed 10% of the global budget where the eligible expenditure is less than 80% of the global budget. … the percentages indicated above are not intended to operate as a minimum-level fee rate for production services.

figures.finding: 20 Screen Ireland-supported films were released in cinemas in 2024; that year it advanced €22.5 million in production loans, took back €0.7 million in recoupment and provided €21.5 million against loans it does not expect repaid.
figures.applies: Ireland, Screen Ireland Annual Report 2024 (financial statements, €000s); recoupment in a year relates to earlier loans, so the ratio is a proxy.

sources.said: Throughout the year, 20 Screen Ireland-supported films were released in cinemas … Advanced during the year 22,487 3,417 25,904 … Recoupment during the year (707) (782) (1,489) … Provision for year (21,476) (2,900) (24,376) … A provision is made based on the likely percentage of loans which will be repaid

figures.finding: Screen Producers Ireland represents independent producers in negotiations with government, broadcasters, funders and unions; membership is €500 a year (€225 for an emerging producer).

sources.said: we represent our members in discussions and negotiations with the Government, state bodies, broadcasters, funding agents and trade unions. … Standard Membership €500 per annum … Emerging Producer Membership €225 per annum

figures.finding: In 2021 Screen Ireland decided 26 applications for Irish (feature) production funding and funded 19; across all production schemes 83 of 122, and 63 of 120 feature film development applications.
figures.applies: Ireland, Screen Ireland decisions made 1 January to 31 December 2021 (later annual reports, 2022-2024, publish no such table).

sources.said: This information relates to projects that were assessed and decisions made between 1st January and 31st December 2021. … Feature Film Development 120 63 … Irish Production 26 19 … Creative Co-Production 10 7 … Total 122 83
